title: Acquire an operator law with its defect, then compile scoped corrected programs
statement: For fixed exact-rational linear primitives A,B with vector and transpose actions, bounded law/rank acquisition plus fresh all-input identity checks can retain a relation AB=q BA+cI+UV^T and degree-filtered defect modules. Conditional on the accepted identity, the modules compile later bounded-degree programs into ideal normal forms and exact corrections, and expose their common or program-specific validity domains. When rank-one discovery is unsupported, a separately acquired small faithful operator algebra is an alternative; otherwise return UNKNOWN.

requires: A fixed finite-dimensional exact-rational linear-action API for A and B.
Transpose-action queries for the same fixed primitives.
An explicit word library, rank/search budget, and degree/circuit cap; alternatively, an explicit small-algebra dimension budget.
Fresh independent validation vectors drawn after adaptive discovery data, with the declared candidate-level confidence allocation.
provides: An acquired low-rank identity R=UV^T with a randomized all-input certificate and explicit false-accept bound, or a checked finite multiplication table for a small closed algebra.
For a defect law, retained left/right defect modules, corrected normal forms for later bounded-degree programs, and exact correction/validity calculations without new native acquisition calls.
A fail-closed UNKNOWN result when the search, uniqueness, module degree, or algebra-closure budget is unsupported.
assumptions: The source maps are exactly linear, rational, and unchanged between acquisition and reuse; these semantics are supplied or justified externally, not learned from finitely many queries.
The q-law executor supports only the declared law shape and bounded degree. The rank-one uniqueness gate is scoped to its fixed word library.
Conditional correctness follows from the accepted identity/closure event; numerical noise, nonlinear or drifting maps, and physical interfaces are excluded.
costs: Source-reported controls include n=64, degree-eight acquisition in 68 actions versus 128 tomography; n=32 q=2 acquisition in 96 versus 64 tomography, followed by zero new synthesis calls and 4 B execution actions versus 12 direct; kinetic 250 versus 192, Chebyshev 86 versus 80, and fermionic closure 96 versus 40.

Each vector response contains n field elements; rational arithmetic, bit growth, stored bases, correction tables, macros and primitive costs must be charged. No total-cost or retaining-method superiority follows.
contract.units: Primitive vector-action calls; each action returns an n-entry rational vector. Returned elements, arithmetic, bit growth, memory, and macro expansion are separate costs.
contract.obstruction: No guarantee for an arbitrary source that does not meet the declared relation/closure budget. The projection P x^2 P differs from (P x P)^2 in the Chebyshev example, so the procedure is not a physical force-law acquisition. Scalar-query lower bounds do not transfer to vector/transpose access. No priority or practical-advantage claim is established.

body:
1. Fix the primitive set and declared bounded word/rank/circuit grammar. Reuse one exact action/transpose observation record.
2. For the specialized law route, compress AB-sigma BA, recover c from the repeated characteristic-polynomial root under n>2r, obtain a candidate residual factorization from vector and transpose actions, and freshly check the factorization on independent vectors.
3. For structural rank-one discovery, linearize the 2x2-minor equations over the fixed quadratic word library. Full coefficient rank rules out rank-one laws only there; a unique decomposable kernel proves uniqueness in that library conditional on fresh native certification. Higher kernel dimension returns UNKNOWN.
4. Propagate acquired factors into degree-filtered left/right modules. For degree cap L, their row module gives the maximal common subspace protected under every allowed use of the acquired law.
5. Normalize each later program to an ideal normal form plus a compact correction matrix. Compute equality and the kernel for a specific uncorrected procedure when the comparison is represented; synthesize corrected procedures with no new native acquisition calls.
6. If a small faithful operator algebra is observed instead, fit and jointly check all generator closure relations. Conditional on closure and observed independence, its retained table evaluates every finite program in the same primitives.
7. When neither representation is certified, return UNKNOWN. Do not infer source semantics, higher-degree/rank laws, physical behavior, or general advantage from the finite search.
